sources: Names and definitions, checked against two independent written sources: Wikipedia, 'Fielding (cricket)' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_(cricket) (names as an angle word plus a distance word; silly, short, deep, long; square; slips numbered outwards from the wicket-keeper; positions 'neither fixed nor precisely defined') and 'Glossary of cricket terms' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cricket_terms (cover, fine, cordon); and SportPlan, 'Cricket Fielding Positions Explained' https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Cricket/guides/cricket-fielding-positions-explained.jsp (sides, square, slips, gully, third man, mirrored for left-handers).

Law 28.4 (Limitation of on side fielders): MCC Laws of Cricket, 2017 Code (3rd edition 2022), Law 28 'The Fielder' https://www.lords.org/mcc/the-laws/the-fielder (also quoted by Wisden, https://www.wisden.com/series/australia-in-england-2024/cricket-news/england-concede-rare-bodyline-no-ball-for-illegal-leg-side-field-placings); ICC Men's Test Playing Conditions clause 28.4 https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/mens-test-match-clause-28-the-fielder and Men's ODI clause 28.4.2-28.4.3 (striker's end umpire calls no ball) https://icc-cricket.com/news/mens-odi-match-clause-28-the-fielder. The 'on side' is the leg side for the batter.

MCC published a 2026 edition of the Laws, in force from October 2026 (https://www.lords.org/getmedia/72990a68-98cd-4c6e-89ac-a2dce54533ad/Ten-major-changes-to-Laws-for-2026-edition_5.pdf); its ten headline changes do not touch Law 28, but the full 2026 text was not read, so check the clause number against the current edition. Field plans are illustrative, for a right-handed batter (mirrored for a left-hander). Figures: make_dyk_fielding.py.

short.vo: Silly mid-off. Deep backward square leg. Third man. Cricket's fielding names sound like nonsense. They are not. They are a code, and once you can read it, you can read any field.
The first word is an angle, seen from the batter. Point, cover and mid-off sit on the off side. Mid-on, mid-wicket and square leg sit on the leg side.

scene.title: Word one: the angle
scene.sub: off side on the right, leg side on the left
note: leg side: mid-on · mid-wicket · square leg

short.vo: The second word is the distance. Short means closer to the batter. Deep, or long, means farther. And silly means so close that it is dangerous, only a few metres from the bat.

scene.title: Word two: the distance
note: short = closer · deep or long = farther

short.vo: Square means level with the batter, across the pitch. Fine is the opposite: behind the batter, close to the line of the pitch. So fine leg is behind square on the leg side, and third man is its partner on the off side.

scene.title: Square and fine
scene.sub: across the pitch, or behind it
note: fine = behind, near the line of the pitch

short.vo: Close to the keeper, slips are numbered outwards. First slip, second slip, third slip. Together, the slip cordon. The gully stands a little squarer, on the off side.

Here is the twist. Fielders cannot stand anywhere. Law twenty-eight point four says that when the bowler delivers, no more than two fielders, besides the keeper, may be behind the batting crease on the leg side. A third there, and the umpire calls no ball.

scene.title: Law 28.4
scene.body: At the instant of the bowler's delivery there shall not be more than two fielders, other than the wicket-keeper, behind the popping crease on the on side.
scene.margin: A breach is a no ball.

short.vo: Everything else is the captain's call. The names are loose labels, not fixed spots, and for a left-hander, every side flips.

scene.title: Not fixed
scene.body: Positions are neither fixed nor precisely defined. The captain moves them for the bowler and the batter, and a left-hander reverses the sides.
scene.margin: So a field is a plan, not a map.

short.vo: Now you can read any field. Next match, try naming every fielder before the commentator does. Subscribe to The Third Man on YouTube for more Did You Know.

short.title: Fielding Positions Explained: How to Read Any Field | Did You Know Ep 2 #Shorts
short.description:
Fielding positions explained: how to read any cricket field. Names are a code: an angle word (cover, mid-wicket, point, square leg) and a distance word (short, deep, long, silly). Slips are numbered outwards from the wicket-keeper. Then the twist: Law 28.4 says no more than two fielders, besides the wicket-keeper, may stand behind the batting crease on the leg side when the bowler delivers; a third is a no ball. Positions are loose labels, not fixed spots. Illustrative field plans for a right-handed batter.

Sources: MCC Laws of Cricket (Law 28.4, 2017 Code, 3rd edition 2022), ICC Playing Conditions clause 28.4, Wikipedia (Fielding (cricket); Glossary of cricket terms), SportPlan's fielding positions guide.
